quote: Our work leverages recent breakthroughs in foundation models for voice cloning... enabling us to generate high quality speech while applying fine-grained emotion controls.
The ultimate objective in the field of conversational systems is to develop intelligent agents capable of comprehending, deciding, and synthesizing speech with nuanced emotional undertones.
We follow previous voice cloning work on measuring word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM).

We use ... to calculate WER and SIM. For WER, we first transcribe the generated clips with Whisper-large-v3 and calculate WER with jiwer library ... We use the WER of audio generated without any emotion control (original voice cloning model) as a baseline ... Similar SIM between emotion‑controlled audio and baseline suggests our framework preserves speaker identity.
We use 100 texts from Common Voice dataset to calculate WER and SIM. For WER, we first transcribe the generated clips with Whisper-large-v3 and calculate WER with jiwer library (nikvaessen).

We asked one question for each emotion and each metric to 23 university student volunteers from our lab and recruited on campus. Participants are told that responses are used to evaluate a new emotional text-to-speech framework.
guideline: Participants compare audio samples and select which better conveys the emotion based on evaluation metrics such as ESA, EEA, EDT, EIT, ESC, EEC, EST.

Participants were presented binary choice questions for each metric (e.g., which sample better conveys the emotion) and instructed that responses would be used to evaluate the new emotional TTS framework.

Participants compare audio samples with and without control generated from emotion-neutral text, selecting which better conveys the emotion. ESA measures the percentage choosing the controlled audio and tests the system's ability to embed any emotions to any text.
